Who has Halloween broadcast?


50 minute headline set!

Free tickets

Faygo break!

80 different clothing items at merch - does KISS, Iron Maiden or Rolling Stones even have that many? Combined?

A lot more young people than imagined though maybe Juggalos don't live past 40. Even little kids.

Sometimes I wish I was born and raised a Juggalo instead of a late in life convert after watching Woodstock '99 10 years after the fact. 2nd only to The Who as the best Woodstock set ever.

Jugalettes so sexy


When I got there I saw they weren't going on til 10:40, found a 4 story consignment mall 2 blocks away. Spent almost 2 hours there. I don't buy stuff anymore but figured if I spent enough time there I would. Ended up getting Alvin Lee Ten Years Later @ Rockpalast and The Life And Times Of Steve Marriott on DVD for $16.21 total. There was a casket on the 4th floor that smelled new. Only $875. I think I will get that and paint my own KISS logo. What's Gene gonna do dig me up and take it back?

(this is a slightly edited transcript from episode 3 of the very short lived Songs And Stories From The I Just Want To Have Something To Do Archives on the now discontinued Past Lives Radio, except that included a few musical interludes.)

Recording so-so, no wind screens, mics mighta been under the shirt, knew it was covered and there would soon be pro shot video so it was all about the experience to me.

My first ever Phish show.

Not that I was ever against them specifically, just from the earliest days on the internet and usenet, their fans and Deadheads were the most annoyingly sanctimonously people.

They are a massive touring juggernaut but exist completely outside the mainstream. I am not aware of any Phish song ever played on FM radio in the 1990's. As a matter of fact, this may be hard to believe but until Friday I had never heard a single Phish song.

Of course a show like this wouldn't even be on the radar if not for my fascination with the secondary market. Last time they did a 3 nighter at the Bowl, Friday bottomed out at a very low price. No way that happens again, the resellers will get smart about it right? Yet the last lowest price on Tickpick was around $17 and I paid $20.

Walking up Highland Ave toward Hollywood Bowl there are ever more street vendors, now just setting up full bars on the sidewalk and the disturbing site of Nitrous oxide tanks and balloons. I have heard about the Nitrous Mafia and saw some of it for the first time outside the Billy Strings show 2 years ago. I had a pretty visceral reaction. I did it once when I was 16 and still worry I have permanent brain damage.

The closer I got to the Bowl the more it resembled Skid Row. Not the band but the downtown LA dead end known for massive homeless encampments and out of control drug dealing and abuse.

Inebriation and overconsumption has been associated with concerts back to the beginning and throw in cannabis and psychedelics and that's what the uninitiated might think belongs at a Phish show. It's a little darker than that. On the walk up the hill it was clear almost everyone was on something.

I have been to skid row, lived around the corner from a crack spot and see daily drug use on the streets and public transportation but never anything quite I was witnessing here.

Imagine the most fucked up person still in the bar at closing time? That's more than half the people on the walk. They never pass out because they're on cocaine and inhalents. Some people aren't on illegal drugs but the show the effects of all day drinking to prepare for the show.

I almost just split but made it this far and decided to just forge ahead. At least it looks like the skeeziest elements aren't even coming inside. Once I set the budget of $20 it was so easy to get a ticket as many people outside can't even pay that.

I was walking in next to someone who still had a spare. Standing on top of the benches right before the entrance is a lot lizard. From a distance she might be mistaken for a free spirited hippie chick instead of a slave to substances . She throws her finger in the air, her hairy armpits almost in my face but with a blank stare and black saucer pupils and says in a monotone "I Need a ticket." Won't pay $20.

And later on inside while I was already making that judgement call, I was on the stairs smoking my first joint in a few weeks trying to get into the groove when I was faced with an 8 year old's look of disgust. I bet the kids grows up hating Phish and his parents.

The show starts off with a guitar riff and the music is enjoyable but the first set a little too chill and still background music for various onsite social events.

I know I am not the only one who has expressed an opinion without listening to the music so I will do my best to explain.

It's mostly rock music with a jazz presentation and room for improvosation even if seeminly every show clocks in at 3 hours even. The show is streamed at home either on Pay per view or subscription basis. I was in section L row 1 so I could watch the video screen they are playing as much for the cameras as the assembled crowd.

So following a Phish tour from home is like binging a Netflix series except for live music. You are never getting the same show twice.

Apparently the first time the band gained any industry recognition was when they were seen moving up the Pollstar concert charts which tracks ticket sales. Also they are more underground and grass roots than the most of the "punk" and alternative on the radio in the 1990's as they made it all the way to the arena level completely under the radar.

If Metallica didn't put out that one album designed for FM radio and MTV they might have had a parallel career arc.

The second set performed after sunset flowed a lot better and some of the music had some more interesting elements even including a bit of metal within one of the jams.

Not sure I a would go again but glad I experienced it at least once. But if my life took any alternate detours into different subcultures I would still rather be a Juggalo.

If you like concerts as much as me I would recommend checking them out should the opportunity arise. You don't have to go to every show, spreadsheet the setlist or suck down nitrous oxide.

I am not into endless jams or making a career out of listening to a band because it's a different show every night. Even if I keep referencing dopamine triggering setlist changes from time to time. But the music was really good. They are obviously highly accomplished players. Some of the songs can be trimmed down to 3 to 5 minutes and be quite the toe tappers.

One of the reason I don't go to as many Hollywood Bowl shows is whether it's shuttle or car there is just no easy way out of there. Even on foot to the Metro the sidewalk is so clogged with hot dog vendors there are massive bottlenecks.

The reimagined parking lot has now allowed for a wide pedestrian walkway behind the fence between the sidewalk and Highland Avenue allowing us to walk unhindered.

On the way out there were more nitrous sales and a popping balloon caused a loud "Oh fuck" response from me. A zombie with a tank said "You Have PTSD too!"
